hypothesis: Light eth_call spends ~47% of server CPU in futex wait/wake on tokio's blocking pool (one mutex + condvar per spawn, finish and park), independent of how many calls are in flight (exp-blockio-8 had no effect). Running the spawn_blocking_io closure on the rayon RPC pool (per-worker deques, spin before sleep) should cut the light phase substantially; heavy calls are CPU-bound per call and should be flat or slightly better.
llm_commentary: Moving spawn_blocking_io from tokio's blocking pool to reth's rayon RPC pool (prototype commit d7c8d5c1c6) is the largest single win: c8a 5.00→4.67s (-6.6%), c8i 6.41→5.47s (-14.7%), c8g 7.51→6.72s (-10.5%), all with disjoint run ranges and test.sh's exact eth_call outputs passing. It confirms the light-phase profile: the ~47% futex wait/wake was the per-call handoff through tokio's single blocking-pool mutex and condvar (unaffected by --rpc.max-blocking-io-requests), and rayon's per-worker deques plus spin-before-sleep avoid most of it; Intel gains most, consistent with its costlier cross-core wakeups. Cumulative against the bare baseline: -12.9% c8a, -23.7% c8i, -24.5% c8g. Before relying on it: the prototype shares the pool with debug_trace*/spawn_tracing work (bounded only by its own guard), no longer races calls against node shutdown, and the light/heavy split of this gain is unmeasured with profiling off, so a symbolized profile and a mixed tracing+eth_call check are the next steps.
